referencePatternsToCopy.label: Event detail and RSVP flow
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy an event detail layout: title, date/time, location, host, capacity/status chip, attendee context, RSVP action, and confirmation state.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

findings.title: Action/review states are still dimmed modal-style screens rather than durable product states
visibleEvidence: Contact sheets show most action-or-review rows with a darkened backdrop and centered/panel overlay; the user is reviewing a transient workflow step rather than a normal full-bright product screen.
findings.description: Pass 33 fixed the missed B20 capture and added stronger domain copy, but action screens still read as modal workflow confirmations. Production UI needs editable, persistent composer/detail/review states that are usable as screens, not dimmed evidence overlays.
concreteRequiredFixes: Render action/review states as full-bright product routes or sheets with normal navigation chrome, not dimmed modal overlays.

For event, announcement, payment, approval, marketplace, document, social, and export workflows, make the action screen show editable content, context, preview/status, and clear primary/secondary actions.
Recapture action rows and prove the screenshots are no longer darkened or visually secondary to a background page.
findings.requiredFix: Replace dimmed action modals with durable full-bright product action surfaces and recapture all action rows.
acceptanceChecks: No action-or-review screenshot is visibly dimmed behind a modal overlay.
Each action state exposes the workflow object, editable/reviewable details, primary action, alternate/change/cancel path, and post-action state preview.

findings.title: Many utility flows still look like status/checklist panels instead of product-native screens
visibleEvidence: Export, ad-off, social, chess, connection, and data rows repeatedly show stacked step lists or account-state cards rather than file browsers, message inboxes, chess board/score sheets, billing settings, or document/product surfaces.
findings.description: The UI has more domain language but several surface families remain rendered through a generic status-panel grammar. A production app needs a message thread, document viewer/list, export package workspace, ad-free billing settings, chess match/club board, and marketplace/listing browser to look structurally different.
concreteRequiredFixes: Create distinct renderer layouts for export/data workspace, message inbox/thread, ad-free billing/entitlement, chess board/match result, documents, and marketplace browsing/listing.
Use tables/lists, previews, receipts, files, boards, and threads where appropriate instead of checklist-like step cards.
Update screenshots to demonstrate the structural difference, not just different text labels.
findings.requiredFix: Replace generic status/checklist utility panels with surface-specific product layouts.
acceptanceChecks: Utility workflows cannot share the same stacked checklist visual structure as RSVP/payment/request cards.
Each utility family has a recognizable product layout matching its job-to-be-done.

findings.title: Tabbed information architecture is visible but not yet proven as a persona-customized navigation model
visibleEvidence: Bottom tabs appear on many rows, which is progress, but evidence mostly captures Home/action workflow rows. It does not yet prove customized tabs per persona, pinned surfaces, Messages tab behavior, or minimized/medium/expanded surface navigation across examples.
findings.description: Pass 33 shows the navigation shell exists, but B25 needs proof that the app experience is organized by community/product jobs rather than only by a captured workflow card. The evidence needs explicit tab screens and pinned/minimized/expanded card states.
concreteRequiredFixes: Add B25 evidence rows for each community/persona home tab, Messages/Communication tab, at least one custom tab, pinned card surface, minimized card, medium in-focus card, and expanded card.
If the UI cannot produce those states, implement the missing state support before recapture.
Tie tab labels and card grouping to the community-specific product docs.
findings.requiredFix: Capture and, if needed, implement persona-specific tabs, pinned surfaces, and card size states as first-class product navigation.
acceptanceChecks: Fresh evidence includes Home and Messages tabs for every example community.
At least one persona-custom tab and pinned surface is visible for each relevant community.
Minimized/medium/expanded states are visible and not inferred from code.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycle controls improved but are not complete or screen-specific enough across all primary flows
visibleEvidence: Several rows now include change/edit/preview language, but not every primary workflow visibly proves reject/withdraw/cancel/reopen/history/receiver continuation as appropriate to that domain.
findings.description: The lifecycle follow-up panel is useful, but it is still a generalized appendage in many workflows. The judge needs to see domain-specific lifecycle paths: RSVP change/cancel/waitlist, approval approve/reject/request changes/reopen, equipment reserve/return/delist/queue/current holder, document open/download/acknowledge/version, and payments retry/refund/receipt.
concreteRequiredFixes: For each primary workflow, define domain-specific lifecycle actions and show them in entry/action/result screenshots.
Avoid a universal lifecycle panel unless its actions are mapped to the domain object and visible state.
Update product docs and card-surface mappings when lifecycle paths are missing.
findings.requiredFix: Make lifecycle actions domain-specific and visible in screenshots for every primary workflow.
acceptanceChecks: Workflow scorecards name the expected lifecycle actions and cite visible screenshot rows.
No primary workflow relies only on accept/cancel or a generic change option.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycle UX is incomplete
findings.summary: 6 workflow/persona lifecycle scorecards failed. The UI is still proving action-card completion rather than full production workflow lifecycles.
findings.requiredFix: Use the failed lifecycle scorecards to add concrete objects, decision information, semantic primary and alternate actions, persistent result state, and receiver/continuation state before recapturing evidence.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the overall UI feel production-grade for the target users, not merely workflow-complete?
visibleEvidence: Contact sheets show richer domain surfaces and bottom tabs, but repeated modal action states and utility panels still dominate many workflows.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: Pass 33 is a meaningful improvement, but the experience is not consistently production-grade yet.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Remove dimmed workflow-modal action states and replace utility/status panels with specialized product screens.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
visibleEvidence: Bottom tabs are visible across rows and visual polish is improved, but the evidence does not prove persona-specific tab organization, pinned cards, or card expansion states.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The shell looks more modern than earlier passes, but navigation proof is incomplete.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Capture and implement persona-specific tabs, pinned surfaces, Messages tab behavior, and minimized/medium/expanded cards.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are main user-facing screens organized around community content and jobs-to-be-done rather than a global workflow/evidence surface?
visibleEvidence: Garden, Masjid, soccer, HOA, and book examples now use recognizable objects, but many utility/social/export/ad/chess screens still read like workflow evidence panels.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: Community content is present; structural product diversity is still insufficient.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Give each major surface family its own product layout and lifecycle model.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, repeated-card, checklist-modal, thin-content, and default-scaffold findings absent?
visibleEvidence: Action/review rows are frequently dimmed; checklist/status panels recur in utility surfaces.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: No severe clipping is visible in the contact sheets, but major repeated-surface and modal-evidence issues remain.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Fix modal/dimmed action evidence and repeated utility panel layouts before closeout.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material detail surface composition
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Build a domain detail page with primary content, metadata, status, and actions instead of a generic task card.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material Design cards and lists
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Use cards/lists only as scannable containers with clear hierarchy, content, metadata, and actions. Do not use repeated cards as the whole primary workflow.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Flutter sample app implementation patterns
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Copy the separation between app shell, route state, domain widgets, and testable UI states rather than hardcoding a single generic renderer.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Material navigation and information architecture
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Organize screens by user jobs and destinations; keep primary actions visible and avoid exposing implementation taxonomy.

referencePatternsToCopy.label: Apple HIG navigation and content organization
referencePatternsToCopy.whatToCopy: Make navigation predictable, content-centered, and appropriate for the user’s current task.

llmVisionReview.summary: Pass 33 improves domain content, tab visibility, and lifecycle wording, but does not yet pass production UX: action states remain modal/dimmed, utility flows still use generic status panels, tab/pinned/expanded navigation evidence is incomplete, and lifecycle controls are not domain-specific enough across all primary flows.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Does the overall UI feel production-grade for the target users, not merely workflow-complete?
visibleEvidence: Contact sheets show richer domain surfaces and bottom tabs, but repeated modal action states and utility panels still dominate many workflows.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: Pass 33 is a meaningful improvement, but the experience is not consistently production-grade yet.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Remove dimmed workflow-modal action states and replace utility/status panels with specialized product screens.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Is the UI modern, easy to use, easy to navigate, and visually appealing for the target persona?
visibleEvidence: Bottom tabs are visible across rows and visual polish is improved, but the evidence does not prove persona-specific tab organization, pinned cards, or card expansion states.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: The shell looks more modern than earlier passes, but navigation proof is incomplete.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Capture and implement persona-specific tabs, pinned surfaces, Messages tab behavior, and minimized/medium/expanded cards.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are main user-facing screens organized around community content and jobs-to-be-done rather than a global workflow/evidence surface?
visibleEvidence: Garden, Masjid, soccer, HOA, and book examples now use recognizable objects, but many utility/social/export/ad/chess screens still read like workflow evidence panels.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: Community content is present; structural product diversity is still insufficient.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Give each major surface family its own product layout and lifecycle model.

holisticQuestionAnswers.question: Are blocking or major overlap, clipping, crowding, repeated-card, checklist-modal, thin-content, and default-scaffold findings absent?
visibleEvidence: Action/review rows are frequently dimmed; checklist/status panels recur in utility surfaces.
holisticQuestionAnswers.critique: No severe clipping is visible in the contact sheets, but major repeated-surface and modal-evidence issues remain.
holisticQuestionAnswers.requiredFix: Fix modal/dimmed action evidence and repeated utility panel layouts before closeout.

findings.title: Action/review states are still dimmed modal-style screens rather than durable product states
visibleEvidence: Contact sheets show most action-or-review rows with a darkened backdrop and centered/panel overlay; the user is reviewing a transient workflow step rather than a normal full-bright product screen.
findings.description: Pass 33 fixed the missed B20 capture and added stronger domain copy, but action screens still read as modal workflow confirmations. Production UI needs editable, persistent composer/detail/review states that are usable as screens, not dimmed evidence overlays.
concreteRequiredFixes: Render action/review states as full-bright product routes or sheets with normal navigation chrome, not dimmed modal overlays.

For event, announcement, payment, approval, marketplace, document, social, and export workflows, make the action screen show editable content, context, preview/status, and clear primary/secondary actions.
Recapture action rows and prove the screenshots are no longer darkened or visually secondary to a background page.
findings.requiredFix: Replace dimmed action modals with durable full-bright product action surfaces and recapture all action rows.
acceptanceChecks: No action-or-review screenshot is visibly dimmed behind a modal overlay.
Each action state exposes the workflow object, editable/reviewable details, primary action, alternate/change/cancel path, and post-action state preview.

findings.title: Many utility flows still look like status/checklist panels instead of product-native screens
visibleEvidence: Export, ad-off, social, chess, connection, and data rows repeatedly show stacked step lists or account-state cards rather than file browsers, message inboxes, chess board/score sheets, billing settings, or document/product surfaces.
findings.description: The UI has more domain language but several surface families remain rendered through a generic status-panel grammar. A production app needs a message thread, document viewer/list, export package workspace, ad-free billing settings, chess match/club board, and marketplace/listing browser to look structurally different.
concreteRequiredFixes: Create distinct renderer layouts for export/data workspace, message inbox/thread, ad-free billing/entitlement, chess board/match result, documents, and marketplace browsing/listing.
Use tables/lists, previews, receipts, files, boards, and threads where appropriate instead of checklist-like step cards.
Update screenshots to demonstrate the structural difference, not just different text labels.
findings.requiredFix: Replace generic status/checklist utility panels with surface-specific product layouts.
acceptanceChecks: Utility workflows cannot share the same stacked checklist visual structure as RSVP/payment/request cards.
Each utility family has a recognizable product layout matching its job-to-be-done.

findings.title: Tabbed information architecture is visible but not yet proven as a persona-customized navigation model
visibleEvidence: Bottom tabs appear on many rows, which is progress, but evidence mostly captures Home/action workflow rows. It does not yet prove customized tabs per persona, pinned surfaces, Messages tab behavior, or minimized/medium/expanded surface navigation across examples.
findings.description: Pass 33 shows the navigation shell exists, but B25 needs proof that the app experience is organized by community/product jobs rather than only by a captured workflow card. The evidence needs explicit tab screens and pinned/minimized/expanded card states.
concreteRequiredFixes: Add B25 evidence rows for each community/persona home tab, Messages/Communication tab, at least one custom tab, pinned card surface, minimized card, medium in-focus card, and expanded card.
If the UI cannot produce those states, implement the missing state support before recapture.
Tie tab labels and card grouping to the community-specific product docs.
findings.requiredFix: Capture and, if needed, implement persona-specific tabs, pinned surfaces, and card size states as first-class product navigation.
acceptanceChecks: Fresh evidence includes Home and Messages tabs for every example community.
At least one persona-custom tab and pinned surface is visible for each relevant community.
Minimized/medium/expanded states are visible and not inferred from code.

findings.title: Workflow lifecycle controls improved but are not complete or screen-specific enough across all primary flows
visibleEvidence: Several rows now include change/edit/preview language, but not every primary workflow visibly proves reject/withdraw/cancel/reopen/history/receiver continuation as appropriate to that domain.
findings.description: The lifecycle follow-up panel is useful, but it is still a generalized appendage in many workflows. The judge needs to see domain-specific lifecycle paths: RSVP change/cancel/waitlist, approval approve/reject/request changes/reopen, equipment reserve/return/delist/queue/current holder, document open/download/acknowledge/version, and payments retry/refund/receipt.
concreteRequiredFixes: For each primary workflow, define domain-specific lifecycle actions and show them in entry/action/result screenshots.
Avoid a universal lifecycle panel unless its actions are mapped to the domain object and visible state.
Update product docs and card-surface mappings when lifecycle paths are missing.
findings.requiredFix: Make lifecycle actions domain-specific and visible in screenshots for every primary workflow.
acceptanceChecks: Workflow scorecards name the expected lifecycle actions and cite visible screenshot rows.
No primary workflow relies only on accept/cancel or a generic change option.
